sbert: Topic modeling with Sentence-BERT embeddings

Source: R/package.R
sbert-package.Rd

sbert fits topic models of texts from their sentence embeddings. A sentence embedding places a text in a space where texts with similar meaning lie close together, whatever words they use (Reimers and Gurevych 2019), so topics found in that space group texts by what they mean rather than by the words they share. Each topic is described by its most typical texts and by its distinctive terms, scored with class-based TF-IDF (Grootendorst 2022). Topics can be fitted to whole documents or to their sentences, clauses, or phrases, compared across numbers of topics by coherence and diversity, and used to assign new texts and give each document a mixture of topics.

The embeddings come from pretrained models, each fixed to one version (see models()). A model is downloaded only when it is first needed, with model_download() or after a prompt in an interactive session, and is stored in the user cache (cache_dir()); nothing is downloaded when the package is installed or loaded. The bundled feedback_embeddings let every topic-model function run without any download.

Models and embeddings

Texts are tokenized by the 'tok' package and encoded on the ONNX Runtime through 'onnxr'; pooling, normalization, and all of the topic modeling are done in R. Each model is fixed to one revision and its files are checked by SHA-256, so every user encodes with the same model.

  • install_runtime() installs the ONNX Runtime library.

  • models(), model_status(), model_download(), load_model(), and load_custom() list, download, and load models; cache_dir(), cache_size(), and model_remove() manage the cache.

  • encode() embeds texts; pool() pools token embeddings; topic_similarity() gives cosine similarities between embeddings; blend() combines segment embeddings with their document's.

Preparing a corpus

  • clean_corpus(), strip_list_markers(), and content_ratio() clean the texts.

  • dedupe() collapses repeated texts and counts them.

  • segment() splits documents into sentences, clauses, or phrases; abbreviations() lists the abbreviations that do not end a sentence.

  • topic_corpus() segments, embeds, and tokenizes a corpus once.

Fitting and choosing topic models

  • topics() fits a topic model.

  • compare_topics() compares numbers of topics and segmentation levels.

  • topic_hierarchy() and reduce_topics() relate and merge topics.

The fits are deterministic: k-means starts from fixed farthest-point centers, so no random seed is involved and the same input gives the same topics.

Describing topics

  • topic_sizes(), terms(), representatives(), and as.data.frame() give the tables of a model; name_topics() names its topics.

  • summary(), coherence(), and topic_diversity() evaluate it; keywords() gives keywords of single documents; stop_words() sets the words left out of the terms.

  • plot() draws sizes, terms, representatives, a fit report, and a map; topic_palette() gives its colors.

Assigning topics to texts

  • predict() assigns new texts to topics.

  • topic_membership() gives soft memberships, and topic_gamma() the mixture of topics in each document.

References

Reimers, N. and Gurevych, I. (2019). Sentence-BERT: Sentence embeddings using Siamese BERT-networks. Proceedings of EMNLP-IJCNLP 2019, 3982–3992. doi:10.18653/v1/D19-1410

Grootendorst, M. (2022). BERTopic: Neural topic modeling with a class-based TF-IDF procedure. arXiv:2203.05794.
